comment: Best professor ever, should be awarded the nicest human being in the world by the UN. Gonna miss him forever and ever.

Prof Simpson is extremely nice. He's caring, and if you participate he will love you. It's obvious he loves teaching Greek Mythology. However, his class is almost entirely lectures, and very boring. He's also unclear with grading. There is reading required for every class, but it's manageable. Grading is based off three essays, a midterm and final

Prof. Simpson is the sweetest. He loves to teach this stuff and that is clear. However, this class can be boring. He lecturers the entire time, with little to no group work. The tests are often on larger concepts, rather than what we read about. He is particular about papers and will not read it before submission. Overall, coursework is light.

I loved Professor Simpson, but his grading is confusing. He often grades you in comparison to other students and provides no real criteria before the assignment is due. He just tells you not to worry. It's ok if you miss a class, as long as you keep up with the readings and communicate with him. Participate and he'll love you. Just ask questions.

Great guy, one of my favorite professors thus far at UR. Stuff like second languages don't come easy to me, but by meeting with Dr. Simpson outside of class, and taking my time with the homework, I've so far been able to keep up! Really excited to continue with him, and pursue a degree in Greek!

Professor Simpson means well and is a generally caring person, yet his class is very dull and he never really explains what he expects from his students on the writing assignments. He often takes off points relatively arbitrarily, without giving a conclusive reason.
He's really cool dude. There was about 2 hours of homework before each class but it wasn't very hard. He's really good about answering questions and responds to emails.

Dr Simpson truly is a caring teacher. He is very understanding and does have a clear passion for the subject which he admits can seem boring or unnecessary at times. His lectures can be boring at times but other than that I would recommend the class.

Very nice guy, and very understanding and sympathetic. However, he is very boring, and voice is droning which makes it very hard to focus. He runs out of things to say and expects the students to lead the class. He needs to provide more interesting ways to present information and also grade more assignments.

Yea he's a nice guy, but he doesn't really teach and is a hard grader. He basically expects the students to run the class and when the class has nothing left to say, he becomes concerned since he doesn't prepare anything for class. Only take the fys if it's the only thing left
Excellent professor to take!
One of the nicest professors I've ever met! Take him!

Nice guy but lectures can be just so boring. It was so easy for kids to just stop paying attention because it didn't really make sense how his lessons related to what we were reading. Also never was sure what he wanted in papers, even after I asked him

Wonderful, intelligent man. He does speak slowly, but it is more that he is considering every word before he utters it. Lectures can be a bit dry at points, but what subject doesn't have its dry points that are necessary for learning the topic? He is very witty and supportive of his students.

Nice guy. Likes to lecture and he can get pretty boring sometimes. The class was hard because I had not read any of the required books before. Lots of reading involved, but not impossible to complete. Three essays and two tests. IT will help if you have prior knowledge of Greek and Roman mythology.

be prepared for the vaguest class ever, prompts are often 'write about something you find interesting in one of the plays'  and then you receive low grades for him not agreeing with you. I'm convinced he actually knows nothing about mythology and answers all question starting "well we just don't know..." repeat his opinions if you hope to do well.
Great teacher and a great person. So long as you do not slack in his class you will do fine, but if you do not do your work do not expect to do well in the class. I hope to take more of his classes.
Very funny guy, likes his papers written a certain way so go to him for help, do the assigned readings, at least a skim. Can form a great relationship with him, REALLY loves his subject matter

Prof. Simpson is a very rewarding instructor. He speaks slowly only so that he can choose the most precise words. He accepts lots of abstract thinking, as long as you articulate it well on papers and in conversation. He seems to be in a good mood all of the time, and rarely becomes irritated. He has high expectations, but he justifies grades well.
He talks very slow and can very often get monotonous and boring, but his sporatic sarcastic or witty remarks make up for it. Pretty easy class, lots of reading, but fairly easy

I really loved Professor Simpson- his speech is very slow and calculated, but it makes for a low stress class. Kind of heavy-ish reading load, but he's very understanding if it doesn't get done. Somewhat hard grader, but very interested in getting to know each student. Highly recommend!

Simspon is a great classics scholar and very patient with students who have difficulty understanding the concepts he's teaching. He challenges students and sets high goals for the class, yet eagerly helps outisde the classroom. He really wants students to learn the material and he's a GREAT professor.

Nice professor, very helpful if you go talk to him.  Grades are 3 essays (not too long), one test and a "final project."  Lectures are sometimes a bit drawn out, he speaks very slowly, but nothing too demanding overall.  Fulfills lit requirement, interesting class

Very nice guy and extremely intelligent prof. Yet, tends to slow down and make the class boring. Probably if he could change his style/pace of teaching,he would be awesome. He knows so much, but needs to communicate better with students in class- not to make it a monologue. Othewise GREAT scholar!
He explains concepts well, but talks slow and you have to pay attention.  High expectations can lead to lower grades than you want, but he's a pretty fair grader overall.
Dr. Simpson is a great guy, but his speech turns some people off.  Tends to speak and think in the abstract a great deal.  He's a solid professor.
No Comments

He is a hard grader, but I would still say he grades fairly. He just has high expectations for every student. He is clear and helpful. The class brought Latin to life as we discussed the literary merit of Latin poetry instead of simply translating it.
excellent professor. teaches you a lot. pretty tough and not lenient on grading. makes himself clear about what he wants and expects.
